issue_context.title: count memory cost for returned []byte or SliceLocation
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement

We have limited the total memory block acquired from membuf.Pool to 16G, but the keys and values type which has their underlying array pointing to membuf.Pool also costs a lot memory so the node may OOM.

![image](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/assets/1689766/65a81ee3-bb74-4f29-8176-700483d516e2)
⬇️
![image](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/assets/1689766/3c5e494e-f862-4d3b-9445-caa8aa90f0b0)
comments: Adding index with global sort encounter OOM. We need to merge the fix to release-7.6. Let me change this issue to bug.

review_comments: seems `n` never bigger than it, and b.smallObjOverheadCache always <= 0?

the initial value of `smallObjOverheadCache` is `0`. For the first invocation `n` is bigger than it and will go through line 187~189. Then the next few invocations `n` is less than `smallObjOverheadCache` so directly goes to line 191.
my fault, i read it as `if n > smallObjOverheadBatch {` 😓

I think for each goroutine, `p.limiter.Acquire()` should be invoked only once? Otherwise, there is a risk of deadlock.

```
Total memory: 10

goroutine 1:
func AllocBytesWithSliceLocation() {
    b.allocBytesWithSliceLocation() // limiter.Acquire(9), ok
->  b.recordSmallObjOverhead()      // limiter.Acquire(2), but 9 + 2 > 10, block
}

goroutine 2:
func AllocBytesWithSliceLocation() {
->  b.allocBytesWithSliceLocation() // limiter.Acquire(9), but 9 + 9 > 10, block 
    b.recordSmallObjOverhead()
}
```

In this lock acquisition pattern we only rely the caller don't have too many concurrency and don't acquire too many memory to avoid deadlock 😂 

We don't know how many []byte will be allocated from the `Buffer` so it can't call `Acquire` only once.
